GoldenGate Integrated Extract

  • Capture name prefixed with a * indicates process (re)started between Begin and End snapshots
  • Begin Lag (sec) - lag in seconds of the most recently captured message when begin snapshot was taken
  • End Lag (sec) - lag in seconds of the most recently captured message when end snapshot was taken
  • Redo Mined value is in number of bytes for the begin and end snapshot interval
  • Extract name suffixed by (S) indicates Extract is using Shared Capture Service
  • Redo Mined information for Extracts using Shared Capture Service is always N/A
  • Bytes Sent, Sent LCRs, and Waiting for Extract information for Shared Captures is always N/A
  • Ordered by Extract Name and Capture Name in ascending order
  • If Capture process is (re)started between Begin and End snapshot, the statistics indicates the value for the last start-up time and end snapshot internal

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Large number of database connections
Impact is 4.15 active sessions, 100% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
A large number of sessions connected to the database instance were detected.
It can cause CPU oversubscription and consequently a severe degredation in
database performance and stability.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 4.19 active sessions, 100% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Reduce the number of sessions connected to the database instance. The
      number of connections to the database instance should not exceed ten
      times the number of CPU cores available to the database instance. It
      should also not exceed ten times the CPU limit assigned by the resource
      manager.
   Rationale
      There were 128 sessions connected to the database instance during the
      analysis period. This is a large number compared to the 2 CPU cores
      available to the database instance.


Finding 2: Sequence Usage
Impact is 3.87 active sessions, 93.29% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Sequence cache misses were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 3.91 active sessions, 93.29% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application or look at top SQL to find hot sequences. Use a
      larger cache size for those sequences. Try avoiding the use of the ORDER
      setting if running RAC.


Finding 3: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 3.71 active sessions, 89.36% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

Finding 4: "User I/O" wait Class
Impact is .97 active sessions, 23.42% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
Waits for I/O to temporary tablespaces were not consuming significant database
time.
The throughput of the I/O subsystem was not significantly lower than expected.

   No recommendations are available.


Finding 5: Log File Switches
Impact is .4 active sessions, 9.55% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Log file switch operations were consuming significant database time while
waiting for checkpoint completion.
This problem can be caused by use of hot backup mode on tablespaces.
DML to tablespaces in hot backup mode causes generation of additional redo.

  4153754668   GGREPL           2          3.76      .01%
  Average of all 3 containers:  2          9985.43   33.33%

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .4 active sessions, 9.55% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Verify whether incremental shipping was used for standby databases.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .4 active sessions, 9.55% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the log files to 2048 M to hold at least 20 minutes
      of redo information.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Configuration" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .63 active sessions, 15.14% of total activity.

Finding 7: Undersized Redo Log Buffer
Impact is .15 active sessions, 3.63% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits for redo log buffer space were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .15 active sessions, 3.63% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the redo log buffer by setting the value of
      parameter "log_buffer" to 32 M.
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "log_buffer" was "8486912" during the analysis
      period.

   Recommendation 2: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .15 active sessions, 3.63% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 299 K and
      the average time per write was 6 milliseconds.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Configuration" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .63 active sessions, 15.14% of total activity.
